cards.explanation: The answer is that Jesus was already in the boat. Mark 4:36 says the disciples took Jesus with them "…since He was already in the boat." So nobody had to fetch Him. They dismissed the crowd, and Jesus was already aboard, so the boat was ready with Him in it.
The answer is True. Mark 4:36 says, "And there were other boats with Him." So this was a little fleet, not a lone boat. The text doesn't tell us who was in those other boats, and I won't guess.

The answer is swamped. Mark 4:37 says the waves were breaking over the boat, "…so that it was being swamped." That's more water coming in than the boat can handle. I bet anybody on board wished they were somewhere calmer.

The answer is False. The disciples did not let Jesus keep sleeping. Mark 4:38 says, "So they woke Him and said, 'Teacher, don't You care that we are perishing?'" Jesus was in the stern on the cushion, and the disciples went straight to Him. I think I would have done the same, and probably a lot louder.

The answer is that they ask Him whether He cares that they're perishing. Mark 4:38 has them say, "Teacher, don't You care that we are perishing?" They woke Him and asked it straight. That's the kind of question you ask when the water is coming in and you're scared. I think it was the loudest question that boat ever heard.
The answer is wind. Mark 4:39 says Jesus "…rebuked the wind and the sea." Then He told them, "Silence!" and "Be still!" He spoke to the wind and the water directly.

The answer is that the wind dies down and it's perfectly calm. Mark 4:39 says, "And the wind died down, and it was perfectly calm." That came after He commanded, "Silence!" and "Be still!" No leftover wind is mentioned. A violent windstorm turned into perfectly calm.
The answer is "Why are you so afraid?" Mark 4:40 has Jesus ask, "Why are you so afraid?" That's His first question. The second one comes right behind it, and it came after the sea was already calm.

The answer is faith. Mark 4:40 has Jesus ask, "Do you still have no faith?" That's His second question, right after "Why are you so afraid?" Two questions, back to back. I think it's a question worth sitting with, friends.

The answer is "Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?" Mark 4:41 says, "Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?" The disciples asked it of one another, overwhelmed with fear, after the sea had gone calm. The text doesn't answer the question right there, so I'll leave it hanging too.
